verified_behaviors: One durable checkpoint-stop request seals an already-drained, file-only Candidate. Publication, optional Workspace CAS, stop receipt and adjacent events commit atomically; historical replay cannot stop a new generation.

PostgreSQL and HTTP contracts cover active human use, another principal connection, original authority, Manage revocation, replacement credentials, competing claims, immutable mode, rollback, late/deferred lease expiry, WAL restart and migration preservation.

The real Artifact daemon recovers an immutable capture after S3/event failure and deleted local spool. SIGTERM joins a claim waiting on the organization lock; the completed checkpoint stops exactly once. Restart schedules zero completed commits.
A physical thread barrier proves capture remains joined after lease renewal fails; its stale result is not published.

Real accepted gVisor execution files survive checkpoint-stop, S3 readback and restoration into a new Candidate using a fresh object cache. Independent signed GETs verify five objects and a separate readonly JuiceFS mount verifies four restored files and independent inodes.
Existing preparation queue phases, five Candidate Artifacts, 17 execution cases, 18 authenticated HTTP downloads and the CSI/gVisor paths pass.
experiment_notes: No repo-sandbox targets were registered; used the previously authorized disposable QEMU fallback with 4 vCPU, 6 GiB RAM and a 24 GiB overlay.

Initial systemd verification lacked the expiry-reaper example and the VM uses ac-k3s.service instead of k3s.service. Verification passed after supplying all dependency unit files, using the existing VM k3s definition under the expected name; no production service or dependency was changed.

The migration-22 regression fixture now creates its historical rows before dropping later schema columns. The current API cannot create data against an intentionally downgraded schema; production behavior was unchanged by this fixture correction.

The first real execution attempt exposed a pre-existing fault-fixture race: file creation was treated as a completed marker write. The fixture now waits for the full marker bytes before killing the controller; the failed attempt is retained and not counted as a successful check.

The second execution attempt completed the execution cases and checkpoint-stop, then correctly rejected a new generation because the fixture Volume reserved exactly one Candidate per case. The fixture now requests one additional generation while preserving old storage reservations and platform limits; the failed run is not counted as successful.

A subsequent run conservatively stopped at startup authorization with no startup grant and zero accepted mutating requests; it produced Unknown, not a false successful completion. No SQL constraint error was logged, and the exact local-guard failure was not exposed. The same code and deadlines were rerun after host checks completed; this intermittent admission refusal remains a reliability limitation.

Another run stopped during watchdog setup in the reaper-missing case, before it could prove the expected ReaperUnavailable reason. The strict assertion was retained. Before the final rerun, all 55 prior watchdog journal deadlines were confirmed expired with no live request watchdog; those journals were retained and a fresh private spool was created. No guard deadline or protection was relaxed.

Further attempts also refused startup or failed the strict concurrent-start assertion. A diagnostic-only build was used and then removed; none of those runs count as final verification. Host pressure was observed at load 101 on 16 logical CPUs while an unrelated workspace built concurrently; this is a plausible contributor, not proof of a specific failure cause. Final source hashes were rechecked after removing diagnostics, and execution was rerun after an instantaneous CPU sample showed spare capacity.
The supervisor OCI image was reused after confirming its source-bound binary hash; it was unchanged in this increment.
limits: Earlier attempts conservatively refused startup/watchdog setup before user execution; their exact transient causes remain unconfirmed. This evidence does not certify startup reliability or throughput.
One Linux VM with isolated HTTP object transport; no production TLS, HA, cross-node, load or power-loss certification.

Concurrency 1-4 and polling 250-5000ms bound one process only. The Artifact live scenario verifies one scheduled checkpoint job and shutdown while its database claim waits; preparation separately verifies two jobs. This is not an Artifact concurrency or throughput benchmark.
Preflight and filesystem work remain joined. Synchronous log output or blocked IO can delay progress/shutdown. The example service timeout is not a physical IO guarantee.

Checkpoint-stop requires no declared Apps, no blocking active use and already-drained execution history. It does not cancel active processes, force stop, capture browser/App profiles or collect retained storage. A Conflict Artifact preserves the exact saved checkpoint without advancing the changed head.
Computer ready=false; public execution unsupported. Volume orchestration, full lifecycle scheduling, runtime/App health, browser/ComputerView and T01-T43 product acceptance remain incomplete.
